exclude.name: eval-quality
exclude.reason: TEA pins it exactly and a human drives that release; the resolution floor's own min-release-age-exclude names it for the same reason.

package-lock.json.label: root policy: allowlist + CC-BY-4.0
package-lock.json.reason: caniuse-lite is browser-support data under an attribution licence, reached only through eslint-plugin-unicorn > core-js-compat > browserslist, so it is a lint-time dependency that no published file carries.

tolerances.reason: sharp's platform binaries are optional dependencies that only the documentation site build loads. The site is private and ships as static HTML, and LGPL-3.0-or-later binds a redistributor of the covered library, which TEA never is. The root graph carries them because docs:build runs astro from the root. Publishing the site as a package withdraws this and the gate fails.

undeclared.evidence: zod-to-ts 1.2.0's own published package.json carries no license field, which is why npm records none in the lockfile entry; that version's manifest is silent rather than differently licensed. The registry's current top-level license field reads MIT (inherited from the 2.x line, published years later), and the repository at github.com/sachinraja/zod-to-ts carries an MIT LICENSE file whose copyright range (2021-2025) covers 1.2.0's 2023 publish date, which is the evidence that ties the reading to the locked version itself rather than to a later release.
undeclared.reason: A transitive dependency of astro 5 whose manifest declares no licence. The licence it is read as is held against the allowlist like every other entry.

entries.claim: the per-suite call counts one eval:all run makes

`test:eval-data` checks that all (\d+) fragment-selection cases are structurally usable

`npm test` chains ([a-z-]+) checks\. That count covers the whole chain: every entry in it is deterministic and credential-free, so the chain and its credential-free subset are the same list\. `npm run test:ci-coverage` derives the count from `package\.json` and prints it\. Six of the ([a-z-]+) keep the rules, guidance, hook, eval data, eval contracts, and documentation aligned:

`tea-index.csv` classifies all (\d+) fragments into three tiers: \*\*core\*\* \((\d+), always loaded\), \*\*extended\*\* \((\d+), loaded when deeper analysis is called for\), and \*\*specialized\*\* \((\d+), loaded only when the case matches, such as contract testing on a real consumer-provider boundary\)\.

entries.claim: one eval:all run's total model calls and their per-suite breakdown

pattern.match: One `npm run eval:all` for one runner spends (\d+) calls: (\d+) fragment selections \(24 cases at two repetitions\), (\d+) routing intents \(18 intents at two repetitions\), (\d+) complete test designs \(two cases at two repetitions\), (\d+) complete reviews \(one call covers all three fixtures, at three repetitions\), (\d+) complete audits \(two evidence bundles at two repetitions\), and (\d+) complete traces \(two cases at two repetitions\)\.

entries.claim: one eval:all run's total agent calls and all three built-in runners' total

pattern.match: `eval:all` uses two repetitions per fragment-selection case and per routing intent, three repetitions for `test-review`, and two repetitions per `nfr` evidence bundle, per `test-design` epic, and per `trace` fixture set\. One runner makes (\d+) agent calls: (\d+) fragment selections, (\d+) routing intents, (\d+) reviews, (\d+) audits, (\d+) test designs, and (\d+) traces\. All three built-in runners make (\d+) calls\.
